title: AI Voice & TTS News Briefing
summary: Covers Tue Nov 17, 7:52 AM to 8:44 AM MT. One new development: AssemblyAI made its AssemblyAI-STT-3.7 speech recognition family generally available, expanding pre-recorded transcription from 18 to 32 languages with native code-switching and a new speaker-separation model claimed to cut errors 29%, at an unchanged $0.21 per hour. It matters mainly as the transcript and speaker-labeling step that feeds dubbing and subtitling. Earlier today's stories (ElevenLabs-Kotoba, France's CNC rule) remain in the Nov 17 7:52 AM briefing.

articles.title: AssemblyAI-STT-3.7 goes GA: 32 languages, code-switching and improved speaker separation at the same price
articles.summary: AssemblyAI released AssemblyAI-STT-3.7, replacing its Universal models for recorded audio: 32 languages (up from 18; the set includes Hindi, Urdu, Marathi, Persian, Hebrew, Vietnamese, Xhosa and Zulu), automatic language detection, native handling of speakers switching languages mid-sentence, and a new speaker-diarization model with a vendor-claimed 29% lower diarization error rate, still $0.21 per hour. Two live variants ($0.30 and $0.45 per hour) cover captions and voice agents. Universal-3.5 Pro is deprecated and will auto-route to 3.7. Why it matters: dubbing and subtitling start with a transcript that labels who spoke; better diarization and code-switching reduce manual cleanup on interviews and multi-speaker video. Accuracy figures are AssemblyAI's own; benchmark on your own audio, and note languages outside the 32 still need the older Universal-2 model.
